data.gist: Authors argue BMAX's smaller injectate volume avoids blood/erythrocyte dilution seen in large-volume BMAC aspirates, which may explain its better OARSI cartilage scores and lower trabecular separation.
data.plain: Conventional bone marrow concentrate (BMAC) discards the marrow's extracellular matrix and is drawn in large volumes (often >120 cc) that get diluted with blood, giving variable products. The BMAX method yields a smaller, more concentrated product with less contaminating blood and red blood cells, which the authors and others have reported can harm MSC properties; they suggest this lower hematocrit may explain the improved cartilage scores, with some support from better trabecular separation on micro-CT.
